## Package jwks

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/jwks"`

Package jwks publishes and resolves the Ed25519 keys capability tokens are signed with, as an RFC 7517 JSON Web Key Set. NewHandler serves an issuer's keys; a verifier resolves a token's kid through a limes.KeyResolver — Static for keys it holds, Remote for an issuer's set fetched over HTTPS and cached. jwkstest checks a resolver of one's own against the same contract.

<a id="jwks.AlgorithmEd25519"></a><a id="jwks.AlgorithmEdDSA"></a>

### jwks.AlgorithmEd25519, jwks.AlgorithmEdDSA

```go
const (
	AlgorithmEd25519 = jose.AlgEd25519
	AlgorithmEdDSA   = jose.AlgEdDSA
)
```

The names a key's entry may give its algorithm (RFC 9864): the alg the tokens it signs name, as limes.SignerConfig.Algorithm writes it. A JOSE library that matches an entry's alg to a token's, Node's jose among them, finds a key only under the name its tokens use.

```go
const DefaultMaxAge = DefaultRefreshInterval
```

<sub>[jwks/jwks.go](../../jwks/jwks.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.KeyIDPrefix"></a>

### jwks.KeyIDPrefix

```go
const KeyIDPrefix = "limes:"
```

KeyIDPrefix opens the kid of every key a limes issuer signs with. A capability is an at+jwt, a type any authorization server's access tokens share, so the kid is what marks a token as signed by a key of limes's: a verifier refuses any other before it looks a key up, and a signer will not sign under one. It cannot stop a key being copied to another issuer; it keeps limes from reading a token signed under that issuer's kid.

<sub>[jwks/keyid.go](../../jwks/keyid.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.ErrUnavailable"></a>

### jwks.ErrUnavailable

```go
var ErrUnavailable = errors.New("jwks: key set unavailable")
```

ErrUnavailable is returned by Remote when it holds no key set recent enough to trust — the endpoint has been failing for longer than MaxStale, or never answered —, when the kid asked for is not in the set it holds while the endpoint is failing, since the issuer may have rotated it in since, and when the caller's context ends while it waits on the endpoint with no set to serve; the context's error stays matchable. The verifier refuses the token with it — an issuer we cannot reach verifies nothing — and, being the server's fault rather than the token's, it matches no ErrUnauthenticated sentinel.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.ErrUnknownKID"></a>

### jwks.ErrUnknownKID

```go
var ErrUnknownKID = errors.New("jwks: unknown kid")
```

ErrUnknownKID is what a limes.KeyResolver returns for a kid it holds no key for. The verifier wraps it in limes.ErrInvalidToken, the token's fault, and it stays matchable, so ops dashboards can tell "we don't know this kid" from "signature mismatch".

<sub>[jwks/keyid.go](../../jwks/keyid.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.KeyID"></a>

### jwks.KeyID

```go
func KeyID(pub ed25519.PublicKey) string
```

KeyID is the kid of a key published with none named: KeyIDPrefix and its RFC 7638 thumbprint. The same key always gets the same kid, wherever it is derived, and two keys never share one.

<sub>[jwks/keyid.go](../../jwks/keyid.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Marshal"></a>

### jwks.Marshal

```go
func Marshal(keys map[string]ed25519.PublicKey) ([]byte, error)
```

Marshal produces a JWKS document for the supplied kid → public key map, with entries sorted by kid so the same key set always serialises to the same bytes (cacheable, diffable, ETag-able). Every entry names AlgorithmEd25519; MarshalAlgorithms names another. A key that is not an Ed25519 public key's length is refused with limes.ErrInvalidRequest.

<sub>[jwks/jwks.go](../../jwks/jwks.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.MarshalAlgorithms"></a>

### jwks.MarshalAlgorithms

```go
func MarshalAlgorithms(keys map[string]ed25519.PublicKey, algs map[string]string) ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalAlgorithms is Marshal with each key's alg named by algs, kid → name: AlgorithmEdDSA for a key whose signer writes EdDSA, so a library that matches the names finds it. A key algs does not name is AlgorithmEd25519's. A name for a kid keys does not hold, or a name that is neither, is refused with limes.ErrInvalidRequest: it would describe no key, or one no token names.

<sub>[jwks/jwks.go](../../jwks/jwks.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Parse"></a>

### jwks.Parse

```go
func Parse(raw []byte) (map[string]ed25519.PublicKey, error)
```

Parse decodes a JWKS document into a kid → public key map. Entries that are not Ed25519 (a future kty), that lack a kid, whose alg, when set, names neither AlgorithmEd25519 nor AlgorithmEdDSA, whose use or key\_ops is not verifying signatures (RFC 7517 §4.2, §4.3), whose key does not decode to an Ed25519 public key, or that are not of the shape a JWK is read in — a member of another JSON type, no object at all — are skipped rather than failing the document (RFC 7517 §5): one malformed or foreign entry must not take every other key — and so every token signed with them — out of service during a rotation. Two Ed25519 keys naming one kid are both skipped; a kid an entry of another kind also names is not (§4.5). A document that is not JSON at all, names a member twice, or has no "keys" array (RFC 7517 §5) is an error: only \`{"keys":\[]}\` withdraws every key.

<a id="jwks.Handler"></a>

### jwks.Handler

```go
type Handler struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Handler serves a key set as a JWK Set document (RFC 7517), the way the Remote on the other end reads it: under its registered media type (§8.5), with a strong ETag of its bytes that answers If-None-Match with 304 (RFC 9110 §13.1.2), and fresh for MaxAge.

```go
func NewHandler(cfg HandlerConfig) (*Handler, error)
```

NewHandler builds a Handler serving cfg.Keys(), refusing no Keys, a negative MaxAge or one under a second, or a MaxAge beside Revalidate.

<a id="jwks.HandlerConfig"></a>

### jwks.HandlerConfig

```go
type HandlerConfig struct {
	// Keys returns the keys to serve, kid → key. Required.
	Keys func() map[string]ed25519.PublicKey
	// Algorithms returns the alg each key's entry names, kid → name, as
	// MarshalAlgorithms takes them: AlgorithmEdDSA for a key whose signer
	// writes EdDSA. Nil, or a key it does not name: AlgorithmEd25519. A name
	// for a kid Keys no longer returns is ignored, and logged, so
	// withdrawing a key never waits on its name being removed.
	Algorithms func() map[string]string
	// Logger logs a name Algorithms gives for a kid Keys does not return,
	// at WARN, and a set the handler cannot serve, at ERROR. Nil:
	// slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// MaxAge is how long a client may keep the set (RFC 9111 §5.2.2.1).
	// Keep it below the time between publishing a new key and signing with
	// it, and between withdrawing an old key and the end of its tokens'
	// TTL. Served in whole seconds, the fraction dropped, so under a second
	// it is refused: it would read as max-age=0, which still lets a cache
	// serve the set stale. Zero: DefaultMaxAge.
	MaxAge time.Duration
	// Revalidate tells clients to revalidate the set on every use instead of
	// keeping it for MaxAge, which it excludes. It is served as no-cache
	// (RFC 9111 §5.2.2.4), not max-age=0: a response stale at once may
	// still be reused stale where a cache is allowed to (§4.2.4), and
	// no-cache allows none. Remote reads either as fresh for no time.
	Revalidate bool
}
```

HandlerConfig configures the handler that serves a key set.

<a id="jwks.Remote"></a>

### jwks.Remote

```go
type Remote struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Remote is a KeyResolver backed by an issuer's JWKS endpoint, for verifiers that run apart from the issuer. It caches the key set, revalidates with ETag, picks up a rotated-in key on first sight of its kid, and keeps serving the last good set through a bounded outage.

A key the issuer withdraws stays accepted until the next refresh, and through an outage for up to MaxStale. For an incident — a signing key leaked — Block refuses a kid at once, whatever the held set says, and Refresh fetches the set now rather than at the next interval.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.NewRemote"></a>

#### jwks.NewRemote

```go
func NewRemote(cfg RemoteConfig) (*Remote, error)
```

NewRemote builds a Remote, refusing with limes.ErrInvalidConfig a config without a URL or whose URL is not https with a host, a negative interval or MaxDocumentBytes, or intervals that do not nest. It does not fetch: the first PublicKey call does, so constructing a verifier never blocks on the network.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Remote.Block"></a>

#### jwks.Remote.Block

```go
func (r *Remote) Block(kids ...string)
```

Block refuses kids from now on, as ErrUnknownKID, even while the held set or the endpoint still has them: for a signing key withdrawn, or leaked, that must stop verifying before the next refresh — or, with the endpoint down, before MaxStale. It holds for the life of the Remote, until Unblock.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Remote.PublicKey"></a>

#### jwks.Remote.PublicKey

```go
func (r *Remote) PublicKey(ctx context.Context, kid string) (ed25519.PublicKey, error)
```

PublicKey implements limes.KeyResolver. A known key from a set past its freshness but within MaxStale is served at once, its refresh started behind it: a slow endpoint delays no request while the set it holds is still good. A caller waits on the endpoint only for a kid the set does not hold, or a set it cannot serve. A kid Block refused is ErrUnknownKID, before the set or the endpoint is consulted.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Remote.Refresh"></a>

#### jwks.Remote.Refresh

```go
func (r *Remote) Refresh(ctx context.Context) error
```

Refresh fetches the key set now, whenever the last fetch was — an operator's call, which MinRefreshInterval does not hold back — and returns the fetch's error, wrapping ErrUnavailable, or ctx's when the caller gives up first. A key the endpoint no longer serves stops verifying when it returns nil. It waits behind a fetch in flight, then fetches again: the one in flight may have started before the key was withdrawn.

<sub>[jwks/remote.go](../../jwks/remote.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.Remote.Unblock"></a>

#### jwks.Remote.Unblock

```go
func (r *Remote) Unblock(kids ...string)
```

Unblock gives back kids Block refused: each is served again as the key set has it.

<a id="jwks.RemoteConfig"></a>

### jwks.RemoteConfig

```go
type RemoteConfig struct {
	// URL of the issuer's JWKS document, e.g.
	// https://issuer.example/.well-known/jwks.json. It must be https.
	URL string
	// Client performs the fetch. Default: a client with a
	// DefaultFetchTimeout timeout. A fetch runs apart from the caller that
	// started it, and is bounded by DefaultFetchTimeout whatever the
	// client allows. Whatever the client's own redirect policy, a redirect
	// to another scheme or host is refused.
	Client *http.Client
	// RefreshInterval is how long a fetched key set is used before it is
	// re-fetched, unless the response's Cache-Control says a shorter time
	// (RFC 9111): its max-age, less its Age, never below
	// MinRefreshInterval. Default DefaultRefreshInterval.
	RefreshInterval time.Duration
	// MinRefreshInterval rate-limits fetches. A token with an unknown kid
	// triggers a refetch (that is how a newly published key is picked up),
	// but at most once per this interval, so a stream of tokens with
	// made-up kids cannot turn the verifier into a request amplifier
	// against the issuer. Default DefaultMinRefreshInterval.
	MinRefreshInterval time.Duration
	// MaxStale is how long the last good key set keeps being served while
	// fetches fail. Past it the resolver fails closed with
	// ErrUnavailable. Default DefaultMaxStale — comfortably longer than the
	// capability TTLs, shorter than a key's useful life after withdrawal.
	MaxStale time.Duration
	// MaxDocumentBytes caps the response body. Default
	// DefaultMaxDocumentBytes.
	MaxDocumentBytes int
	// Now is the clock; tests override.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Logger logs each fetch — a new or confirmed set at DEBUG, a failure
	// at WARN while the held set is still served and at ERROR once none is —,
	// a fetch skipped inside MinRefreshInterval at DEBUG, Block, Unblock and
	// Refresh, and each kid refused for being blocked. Nil: slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

RemoteConfig configures a Remote. Only URL is required. The intervals must nest: MinRefreshInterval ≤ RefreshInterval ≤ MaxStale.

<a id="jwks.Static"></a>

### jwks.Static

```go
type Static struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Static is the in-memory implementation used in tests and single-node deploys. Maps kid → public key; concurrency-safe via a sync.RWMutex so rotation can swap a kid without restarting callers.

<sub>[jwks/static.go](../../jwks/static.go)</sub>
<a id="jwks.NewStatic"></a>

#### jwks.NewStatic

```go
func NewStatic(cfg StaticConfig) (*Static, error)
```

NewStatic builds a resolver over cfg.Keys, refusing with limes.ErrInvalidConfig an empty kid or a key that is not an Ed25519 public key's length — which the verifier would otherwise read, token by token, as the tokens' fault.

#### jwks.Static.RemoveKey

```go
func (r *Static) RemoveKey(kid string)
```

RemoveKey withdraws a kid. Rotation step 3: call it only once the longest outstanding TTL signed under that key has elapsed.

<sub>[jwks/static.go](../../jwks/static.go)</sub>

#### jwks.Static.SetKey

```go
func (r *Static) SetKey(kid string, key ed25519.PublicKey) error
```

SetKey adds or replaces a kid → key mapping. Rotation step 1: publish the new key alongside the old. It refuses what NewStatic refuses.
